To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the synergistic effect of colistin-based combinations against carbapenem resistant K. pneumoniae is mainly determined by the MIC of colistin.

colistin in combination with either meropenem or tigecyclin showed synergistic activity against all tested carbapenem-resistant Klebsiella isolates, whereas the combination of colistin, meropenem and tigecyclines was not synergistic.
colistin based combination therapy with a β-lactam and tigecyclin might be sufficient and synergistic for all tested carbapenem-resistant K. pneumoniae strains.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the evaluation of colistin-based triple combinations against K. pneumoniae.
the evaluation of different combination regimens against K. pneumoniae.
the development of a three dimensional checkerboard synergy analysis for K. pneumoniae strains and its application for colistin combination therapy.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
colistin based triple combinations are not more effective than double combinations and therefore, should not be used in clinical practice.
colistin should always be used in combination with a β-lactam or tigecyclin against K. pneumoniae.
colistin should only be used in combination with other effective antibiotics in the treatment of carbapenam-resistant Klebsiella infections.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
colistin should not be used as a monotherapy but rather in combination therapy.
colistin based combination therapies with carbapenem or tigecyclin are effective against K. pneumoniae strains with high MICs against all of the drugs, but not for strains with low MICs.
a colistin-based triple combination is not superior to a colistin based double combination against KPC- producing Klebsiella isolates.
The main takeaway from our work is that
colistin based double combinations are effective in treating K. pneumoniae strains with different resistance mechanisms.
the combination of colistin with meropenem and tigecyclide is synergistic in most cases and that the combination of meropenem with tigecyclin is antagonistic in most cases.
colistin based triple combinations might be more beneficial than colistin based double combinations for strains with high MICs against all of the tested antibiotics.
